FINDING_ID: MM_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.94  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.90  
DESCRIPTION: The appendix’s Capability Fingerprint definition in §7.9 is still materially inconsistent with `dynamic_management.py`. The appendix defines `(D_decay, v̄, A, C)` as `(decay rate from best-fitting decay model, mean verification score, total novel verified findings, coverage = A / estimated total real findings)`. The code defines/updates them as `(duplicate ratio, fraction verified, mean severity, distinct flaw classes / classes seen this round)`. This is not a minor proxy substitution; all four components have changed semantics, units, and ranges. The comment in `CapabilityFingerprint` claiming alignment with §7 is therefore false, and any role assignment or live routing based on these values is not implementing the appendix model.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either (a) revise §7.9 to explicitly declare the code uses operational proxies `D_decay_proxy`, `v̄_proxy`, `A_proxy`, `C_proxy` and stop claiming direct implementation, or (b) change the code to compute the appendix quantities: Duane-derived decay, verification score from §7.8, novel verified finding count, and convergence-estimated coverage denominator. Also rename fields if proxies are retained.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.91  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.84  
DESCRIPTION: The “NO FIX NEEDED” decision for convergent finding 4.3 is not fully defensible as stated. `_redundancy_target()` uses total pool size `K = len(self.models)`, but allocation feasibility and admissibility are computed over the active/admissible subset. The note says this is “by design” because the greedy solver handles infeasibility and now logs warnings. That does not remove the model inconsistency: the target is described as desired coverage, but it is knowingly unreachable when PM is excluded or models are inactive. This inflates nominal redundancy requirements, systematically triggers degraded-allocation warnings, and blurs the difference between “true degradation” and “design-induced infeasibility.” The prior resolution addressed operational transparency, not the mathematical mismatch between target definition and admissible capacity.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Redefine redundancy target against admissible active models, e.g. `K_adm(j) = |{m : admissible(j,m) and active(m)}|`, or explicitly split into `r_theoretical(task)` and `r_feasible(task)` in both model and code. If keeping total-pool targeting, document it as an aspirational upper bound, not the operative target.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.89  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.78  
DESCRIPTION: §7.11 Manager Selection is still mathematically disconnected from the implementation. The appendix defines `selected(f) ≡ (Sev(f) > τ_sev) ∧ (S_v(f) ≥ 0.5) ∧ (class(f)=HARD ∨ Sev(f) > τ_soft)`, but the code has no selection function, no `τ_sev/τ_soft`, no `S_v`, and no notion of `class(f)=HARD` on `Finding`. Since `RoundResult.findings` and downstream management operate on unfiltered findings, the appendix currently describes a gate that is not present in the executable system. This is a hard interface discrepancy because it affects which findings are actioned.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Implement `selected(f)` in code with explicit fields for constraint class and multi-verifier score, or mark §7.11 as “specified but not implemented” and remove any implication that the pipeline enforces it.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.87  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
DESCRIPTION: §7.7 Per-Finding Severity remains incompatible with the code data model even beyond the already-reported missing `confidence` field. The formula requires `class(f)` as HARD/SOFT and `V(verification)` as ternary `{True, None, False}`. The code’s `Finding` has `severity: float` precomputed, `verified: bool`, and `flaw_class: int`; it lacks constraint class and cannot represent indeterminate verification separately from false. Therefore the code cannot reconstruct or enforce the appendix severity semantics. This undermines §7.7, §7.8, and §7.11 together.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Extend `Finding` with `constraint_class: Literal["HARD","SOFT"]`, `confidence: float`, and `verification_status: Literal["TRUE","FALSE","INDETERMINATE"]`; compute `severity` from these. If not, rewrite the appendix to match the flattened code representation.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73  
DESCRIPTION: The reduction claim in §6, “Every simpler model in the white paper and this appendix is a special case of G_n,” is too strong as written. `G_n` models combined machine-human detection with human-specific parameters `E, M, α, λ_s, V_s, ρ_MH`. Several appendix constructs are not special cases of this model at all, e.g. parameter uncertainty (§3), severity-loss separation (§4), and format/delivery/decomposition factors (§2) unless additional embedding rules are defined. The statement over-generalises from coverage-family models to the entire appendix.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Narrow the claim to “Every simpler detection-coverage model in the white paper and §1–2/6 is a special case of G_n under additional assumptions,” or explicitly show embeddings for `f_del`, `φ`, `η_dec`, and uncertainty if that stronger claim is intended.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: The asymmetric calibration metric in §6 allows negative values: `κ_asym = 1 − β max(0,E_claimed−E*) − max(0,E*−E_claimed)`. The table includes `−0.125` for a bluffer. But κ is presented as a “calibration metric” alongside symmetric κ in `[0,1]`, and the notation summary does not specify its range or interpretation when negative. Negative calibration scores may be acceptable, but the metric is then not a bounded similarity/calibration coefficient and should not be read like one. This is an edge-case/domain-definition gap.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either define the codomain explicitly as `(-∞,1]`, or clip at 0 and state that severe overconfidence saturates at zero. Also add interpretation for negative values if retained.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.80  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: The online estimator section §7.4 still contains a symbol-level correctness error after prior findings: it says `k(t)` is the local exponential decay rate of `v_w(t)`, then correctly distinguishes it from `λ(t)` in §7.1, but the next standalone sentence says `λ(t) is the empirical decay rate estimated from consecutive round values.` That sentence reassigns the empirical-decay role back to `λ(t)` and contradicts the previous sentence. This is not just notational awkwardness; it changes which quantity enters the estimator and ascending abstraction guard.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace that sentence with `k(t) is the empirical local decay rate estimated from consecutive round values; λ(t) remains the Duane NHPP intensity from §7.1.`  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67  
DESCRIPTION: The appendix claims in §7.10 that `Sev(f)` is “Implemented in pipeline,” but `dynamic_management.py` does not implement the §7.7 formula; it merely carries a scalar `severity` on `Finding`. This is a documentation/interface inconsistency inside the appendix’s implementation status table. A stored field is not equivalent to implementing the formal definition that generates it.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Change §7.10 status to `Represented as input field only; formal computation not implemented here`, or implement the actual severity calculation.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F009  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
DESCRIPTION: The “all formulas in §7–8 were computationally verified using SymPy and Wolfram Alpha” claim near the top is internally overbroad given known unresolved issues inside §7–8 itself, including the still-present `λ(t)`/`k(t)` contradiction and multiple implementation mismatches. Computational verification can validate algebra after formulas are fixed, but it cannot validate contradictory symbol definitions or implementation claims. The statement currently overstates what was verified.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Qualify the claim to “selected algebraic identities and derivatives in §7–8 were computationally checked” and exclude symbol-definition consistency and implementation status from that claim.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F010  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 3  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: The notation summary still contains unresolved symbol ambiguity around `A`. Earlier `A` means anchor state (A0–A3) from the white paper; in the capability fingerprint tuple `(D_decay, v̄, A, C)`, `A` means total novel verified findings. Although context distinguishes them, the same bare symbol is overloaded for conceptually unrelated quantities in the same appendix. This is more than cosmetic because §7.9 then discusses `A` while §1 relation table still extends reports from `(F_n, A)` to `(F_n, R_n, A)`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Rename the fingerprint component to `A_novel` or `N_verified`, and update code/comments accordingly.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F011  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64  
DESCRIPTION: §8.2 defines `Y_union(t) = |⋃ F_i(t)| · H̄_union(t)` but never defines `H̄_union(t)` explicitly. Since `H̄` elsewhere means mean abstraction over a specified finding set, this is inferable, but the strong emergence condition depends on the exact construction of the union benchmark. Without explicit definition, there is avoidable ambiguity about whether `H̄_union` is mean over deduplicated union findings, weighted by contributor count, or computed another way.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Define `H̄_union(t) := mean{H(f) : f ∈ ⋃F_i(t)}` over deduplicated union findings, with the same equivalence relation used elsewhere for finding identity.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F012  
SEVERITY: 0.70  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: The code comment in `CapabilityFingerprint` says “Per-model capability fingerprint (D_decay, v_bar, A, C) from §7. All values in [0,1] or ℝ≥0 as defined in the existing schema.” But `A` in the appendix is a count of total novel verified findings, while role assignment normalises all four dimensions against pool maxima and implicitly treats them as comparable scale features. This is not wrong by itself, but it means the code’s use of `A` as a floating capability component differs from the appendix’s count semantics and should not be described as if directly inherited.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either redefine appendix `A` as a normalised count/rate for routing purposes, or document in code that routing uses a normalised proxy derived from the raw fingerprint, not the raw appendix quantity itself.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F013  
SEVERITY: 0.68  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61  
DESCRIPTION: The implementation-status table in §7.10 says Duane NHPP is implemented in `decay_analysis.py`, but the provided code cross-reference here uses `ConvergenceDetector.estimate_gamma()` in `dynamic_management.py` and its header claims alignment with appendix symbols. Since `estimate_gamma()` is mathematically inconsistent with §7.1 and still present in the active management layer, the appendix should not present NHPP implementation status without clarifying that the management-layer diagnostic is only a proxy and not the formal Duane fit.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Amend §7.10 to distinguish `formal implementation in decay_analysis.py` from `heuristic diagnostic in dynamic_management.py`, or remove the stronger implementation claim until the active layer uses the formal fit.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F014  
SEVERITY: 0.66  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.54  
DESCRIPTION: The phrase in §6, “At ρ_MH = 1, the human adds nothing — their reasoning is fully absorbed into the machine's framing,” is stronger than the formula alone supports. The formula only enforces zero incremental detection contribution under the model, not a literal cognitive claim about “fully absorbed” reasoning. This is rhetorical overreach around a formal parameter and risks conflating model behaviour with psychological interpretation.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Rephrase to `At ρ_MH = 1, the model treats the human stream as contributing no additional independent detection coverage.`  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F015  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57  
DESCRIPTION: The appendix’s definition of `η_dec(i) = |F_decomposed(i)| / |F_full(i)|` is vulnerable to zero-denominator failure if `|F_full(i)| = 0`. This can happen for a weak model, a null artifact area, or simply a full review that found nothing. The text discusses `η_dec < 1` and `>1` but never defines the zero case.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add a convention, e.g. if `|F_full(i)| = 0` and `|F_decomposed(i)| = 0`, define `η_dec = 1` (no evidence decomposition changed yield); if `|F_full(i)| = 0 < |F_decomposed(i)|`, treat as undefined and report absolute counts instead of ratio.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

Definitive stance: the major remaining problems are not new calculus mistakes but unresolved model↔code interface divergences, an over-accepted “no fix needed” decision on redundancy targeting, and a few still-overstated or underspecified claims in the appendix.
